Q: Propagating logging.logger from module to single log file A:

The reason your logs do not appear is due to how Python's logging hierarchy and propagation work.

Key points:

  1. Logger names establish the hierarchical structure.
- In script.py: __name__ == "__main__" → logger "__main__"
- In utils/utils.py: __name__ == "utils.utils" → logger "utils.utils"

2. Propagation:

  • "utils.utils" propagates messages up to the root logger.

  • It does not automatically propagate to "_main_" logger.

3. Handlers:

  • Output messages can only be generated by loggers that are equipped with handlers.

  • The logger in script.py is equipped with a FileHandler, while the logger in utils/utils.py lacks this feature.

    How to fix it

    Option 1: Consistently utilize the root logger.

# script.py
import logging
from utils.utils import load_query

logging.basicConfig(
    filename='etl.log',
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.info("Starting")
load_query()
logger.info("Finished")

How to fix it

Option 2: Let module loggers propagate to the root

 # utils/utils.py
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.propagate = True  # optional, default is True

def load_query():
    logger.info("Running function")

 # script.py
import logging
from utils.utils import load_query

logging.basicConfig(filename='etl.log', level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

logger.info("Starting")
load_query()
logger.info("Finished")

Q: Is it true that in Excel VBA, application.cancel will erase the clipboard if it contains a range? A:

I have developed a workaround.
The following simple code is the first step.

    Dim clipRange As Range
    Set clipRange = Clipboardrange
    
    Application.Calculate
    If Not clipRange Is Nothing Then clipRange.Copy
    Stop

Unfortunately, the subroutine is ugly, but it works.

     Private Function Clipboardrange() As Range
     ' please acknowledge berkeley and associates inc.
         '====================================================================
         ' Returns the Range currently on the Excel clipboard (copied or cut),
         ' assuming:
         '   - The clipboard contains a single-area Range
         '   - The source is in the ActiveWorkbook (or another open workbook)
         ' Returns Nothing if clipboard doesn't contain a range.
         
         ' Strategy:
         '   1. Add temp sheet in ActiveWorkbook.
         '   2. Paste as VALUES into A1 -> get UsedRange size (rows/cols).
         '   3. Clear temp area.
         '   4. Paste again, this time as a LINK near bottom-right of sheet.
         '   5. Read the formula in that cell and use Application.Range()
         '      to get the source range.
         '   6. Resize that top-left range by rows/cols to get full range.
         '   7. Delete the temp sheet and return the Range.
         '   8  restore the clipboard (step 7 empties the clipboard for unknown reasons)
         '      Please note that the restored clipboard might be slightly smaller because it remove cells outside of the usedrange.
         '
         ' NOTES:
         '   - Returns Nothing on failure.
         '   - Uses On Error Resume Next only where specific failures
         '     are expected and commented.
         '====================================================================

    Dim wsTemp      As Worksheet
    Dim nRows       As Long
    Dim nCols       As Long
    Dim oldAlerts   As Boolean
    Dim origMode    As XlCutCopyMode
    Dim origEvents As Boolean
    Dim tempName
    
    If Application.CutCopyMode = False Then Exit Function
    
    If ActiveWorkbook Is Nothing Then Exit Function
    origMode = Application.CutCopyMode
    origEvents = Application.EnableEvents
    Application.EnableEvents = False
    oldAlerts = Application.DisplayAlerts
    Application.DisplayAlerts = False
         Application.ScreenUpdating = False
         
    
    tempName = "__TmpClip_" & Format$(Now, "hhmmss")
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    ' Add temp sheet. In a heavily protected workbook this might fail.
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    On Error Resume Next                    ' EXPECTED: Add may fail if workbook is protected
    Set wsTemp = ActiveWorkbook.Worksheets.Add(before:=ActiveSheet)
    If Not wsTemp Is Nothing Then
        wsTemp.NAME = tempName             ' EXPECTED: Name might clash if called very frequently
    End If
    
    If wsTemp Is Nothing Then GoTo CleanExit
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    ' 1) Paste as VALUES to discover size via UsedRange.
    '    If clipboard does not contain a range, PasteSpecial will fail.
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    On Error GoTo CleanExit                    ' EXPECTED: PasteSpecial fails if clipboard not a range
    wsTemp.Range("A1").PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteValues
    
    With Range(wsTemp.Cells(1), wsTemp.UsedRange)
        nRows = .Rows.Count
        nCols = .Columns.Count
    End With
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    ' 2) Paste again, this time as a LINK, but **near bottom-right**.
    '
    '    Reason:
    '      If the clipboard range is an entire column, Paste Link
    '      will try to write formulas into all 1M+ cells of that column.
    '      By pasting at the bottom-right corner, only a tiny region
    '      is affected, and we still get one formula that tells us
    '      the source range.
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
With wsTemp.Cells(wsTemp.Rows.Count, wsTemp.Columns.Count)
    .Select ' activate cell for Paste Link
    On Error Resume Next    ' EXPECTED: Paste may fail if CutCopyMode changed
           ' this is need to avoid an error 1004 Microsoft Excel cannot paste the data.
    wsTemp.Paste Link:=True  ' only get the first linked cell
    If Err <> 0 Then Stop
    On Error GoTo CleanExit
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    ' 3) read the formula from the first linked cell and turn it into a Range.
    '    Examples:
    '       ='[Book1.xlsx]Sheet1'!$A$1
    '       ='Sheet1'!$B$3
    '       =Sheet1!A:A
    '
    '    Application.Range("Sheet1!A1") (or "'[Book1.xlsx]Sheet1'!$A$1")
    '    will directly give us the Range, so we don't need to parse
    '    sheet/workbook names by hand.
    '----------------------------------------------------------------

    Set Clipboardrange = Application.Range(Mid$(.Formula, 2))
End With
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    ' 4) Now that we know the top-left cell (clipboardrange) and the size
    '    (nRows x nCols), we can compute the full original range.
    '
    '    For whole-column references (A:A), clipboardrange is the whole column,
    '    and Resize(nRows, nCols) shrinks it to the actually-used
    '    rows/columns discovered from the values paste.
    '----------------------------------------------------------------
    Set Clipboardrange = Clipboardrange.Resize(nRows, nCols)
    Set Clipboardrange = Clipboardrange
    Debug.Print "1" & Clipboardrange.Address(, , , 1)
CleanExit:
    On Error Resume Next
    ' Let delete do its normal thing (yes, this clears the clipboard)
    Application.EnableEvents = origEvents
    If Not wsTemp Is Nothing Then
        wsTemp.Delete
    End If

    If Not Clipboardrange Is Nothing Then
        Debug.Print Clipboardrange.Address(, , , 1)
        Select Case origMode
'
            Case xlCopy
                Clipboardrange.Copy
            Case xlCut
                Clipboardrange.Cut
        End Select
    End If

    On Error GoTo 0
    Application.DisplayAlerts = oldAlerts
         Application.ScreenUpdating = True

 End Function
